A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DIVER, with matching research objectives, core methods and experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark evaluations, exploration analyses, reward-shaping ablations and reasoning case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds repeated evaluations, larger-k results, metric validation, reasoning-quality assessments and further robustness experiments.

M1.justification: Table 1 adds DIVER-MIX, explicitly described as combining Textual Diversity and Equational Diversity during training; v1 reports separate TD and ED variants. The underlying GRPO objective, potential-based shaping, clipping and correctness gating remain unchanged. The precise mixing rule is not specified.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OpenR1-Math/NuminaMath training subset, six mathematical benchmarks and three out-of-domain benchmarks. The additional backbone, larger sampling budgets and response-quality assessments do not introduce different datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds the untrained Qwen2.5-Math-7B comparator to the existing Pass@2–32 comparison, which contained only the three exploration baselines and DIVER in v1. The main baseline roster remains unchanged. Renaming GRPO to GRPO w/ Clip-higher in the cross-model table clarifies the comparator already identified in v1's Figure 5.

E3.justification: v2 extends evaluation to Pass@128, 256, 512 and 1024 and adds DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B experiments. New protocols include semantic-similarity comparisons, human-checked equation extraction, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp judging across four quality criteria, and controls using group size 4 and training temperature 0.6. Default training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C.3 and D add equation-extraction error analysis, semantic validation of TD/ED, model-judged reasoning quality and group-size/temperature sensitivity tests; Appendix B.2 adds computational-overhead analysis. These substantially broaden validation beyond v1. The original reward-hacking, horizon and shaping-coefficient analyses remain, with some relocated.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. v2 Appendix C.1 reports three runs, and Table 4 supplies means and standard deviations for in-domain Pass@2–32 results. Out-of-domain columns and larger-k results remain point estimates. The PDFs do not establish v1's run count or specify whether the repeats vary training or evaluation sampling.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes Pass@k Training's reported in-domain/out-of-domain averages from 39.9/58.1 to 41.5/55.3 and adds DIVER-MIX at 43.1/58.8. The Pass@2–32 table replaces in-domain estimates with three-run summaries, such as DIVER's AIME25 Pass@32 changing from 50.0 to 48.9 ± 1.9. Numerous new larger-k, backbone, validation, timing and robustness results are reported; these are additional or revised results, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, reward-shaping derivation, Theorem 1 and Appendix A proof remain unchanged. v2 adds explanatory prose about computing only final-response diversity and explicitly attributes the proof to classical reward-shaping work, without revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about global diversity, deep exploration, policy invariance and reasoning/generalization performance. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of semantic-metric agreement and judge rankings as evidence of meaningful reasoning diversity. It acknowledges imperfect equation extraction while arguing that approximate diversity signals suffice, and discusses computational overhead and robustness. The core exploration explanation and single-turn limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents equation extraction through three LaTeX patterns, re.findall and set-based deduplication. It also reports training times and identifies the semantic encoders and quality judge used in new analyses. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, system prompts and code/data access statements are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds prompt-selection and curriculum approaches through Chen et al. (2025a), Bae et al. (2025) and Qu et al. (2025), alongside several newer RL references. The positioning of DIVER as sequence-level intrinsic exploration remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds localized explanations, acknowledgements and appendix subsections, consolidates supplementary analyses under Appendix D, and updates affiliations and the conference header. The case studies are renumbered rather than rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 substantially extends the displays with tables for timing, larger-k evaluation, extraction accuracy, semantic metrics, quality rankings and hyperparameter sensitivity, plus a reasoning-quality heatmap. Figure 5 expands from three to four models, and the Pass@k table is reformatted for an added comparator and uncertainty estimates. Existing coefficient and horizon plots are relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical scrutiny through repeated-run uncertainty, direct metric-validity checks, robustness tests and clearer extraction details. However, reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: Section 4.3 and Figure 6 retain older Pass@32 values despite Table 4's updates, and Section 4.2's favorable out-of-domain interpretation of Pass@k Training no longer matches its revised Table 1 scores. The added evidence improves assessability, but its integration is incomplete.
